name: ACMR
description: Composite-modulations are widely used in satellite and aeronautical communications, both of which are becoming increasingly congested within the emerging integrated space–aerial–terrestrial paradigm. Automatic Modulation Recognition (AMR) has great potential to enhance these systems, particularly in the presence of signal interference and distortion. However, a significant gap exists due to the lack of publicly available datasets for composite-modulation signals, which hinders the design and validation of AMR methods for satellite and aeronautical applications. To address this issue, we present for the first time a novel automatic composite-modulation recognition (ACMR) dataset comprising 12 types of composite-modulation signals commonly used in current satellite and aeronautical communications. To demonstrate its utility and establish performance baselines for ACMR studies, we design a dual-channel hybrid machine learning model trained on this dataset. We also evaluate state-of-the-art models, which were originally developed for simple-modulation recognition tasks, on our dataset and report their performance alongside our proposed model. Experiment results show that most models achieve over 90% accuracy in the best-case scenario and over 60% accuracy on average, validating the usefulness of the dataset and highlighting our model as the top performer. Furthermore, we test the proposed model on the widely used RML2016.10 A dataset, which contains only single-modulation types, where it achieves a maximum accuracy of 92.41%. These results demonstrate the robustness of both the developed dataset and model, which offer foundational contributions to the advancement of automatic composite-modulation recognition in current and future satellite and aeronautical communication systems.
